mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase 'difference between the number of ... and ...' appears in a statement.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between the number of A and B' as |A - B| (absolute value) instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more than B' (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a phrase 'has N more than' linking two persons.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has N more than B' as A = B - N (reversing the sign).

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When processing a transfer statement, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, using the current counts at that point.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement of the form 'X gives N items to Y' appears.
mathgap.example: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their immediate effect.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When encountering a direct count statement, set the person's count to the given number at that point, overwriting any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement directly assigns a count to a person.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as an immutable initial value and not updating it after later transfers.

mathgap.title: Preserve Difference Order
mathgap.principle: When equating a 'has more than' difference to a 'difference between' two persons, preserve the order of subtraction on both sides (e.g., X - Y = A - B).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational statement equates a 'has more than' difference to a 'difference between' expression.
mathgap.example: Writing X - Y = B - A instead of X - Y = A - B.

mathgap.title: Temporal Evaluation of Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: When evaluating a relational statement, use the current counts of the persons at that point in the text, after any prior transfers or updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational statement appears after some transfers or direct assignments.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a relational statement that appears after they have given away items.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When encountering a conditional transfer, first evaluate the condition using the current counts, and only apply the transfer if the condition holds.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement includes a condition (e.g., 'if X has at least N, then X gives N to Y').
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer without checking the condition.

mathgap.title: Combined Sum Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement gives a combined total for several persons, interpret it as the sum of those persons' counts equals the given total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence says 'A, B, and C together have N items' or similar.
mathgap.example: Interpreting the combined total as each person having N items individually.

mathgap.title: Split Equally Among Recipients (Additive)
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among recipients, set the donor's count to 0 and add the appropriate share to each recipient.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'X splits all their items equally among Y and Z'.
mathgap.example: Forgetting to set the donor's count to zero after splitting.

mathgap.title: Difference Cancellation
mathgap.principle: If an equation equates two differences that share a common term (e.g., X - Y = X - Z), cancel the common term to deduce equality of the remaining terms (Y = Z).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational equation contains the same variable on both sides of a subtraction.
mathgap.example: Failing to cancel the common term in 'Eddie - Irma = Eddie - Janelle' and treating it as a more complex equation.

mathgap.description: Treating 'difference between the number of X and Y' as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to thinking of 'difference' as a magnitude, ignoring the order of the names.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two persons as written and interpret the phrase as a signed subtraction (first minus second).

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as independent constraints rather than as immediate updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer as soon as it appears, updating both giver and receiver counts before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming 'A has N more than B' forces A > B and discarding solutions where A - B is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'more' as a strict inequality rather than a relational equation.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'has N more than' as an equation A = B + N without imposing a positivity constraint on the result.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are only initial conditions, not subject to later modifications.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, overwrite any existing count for that person at that point, even if earlier transfers have altered it.

mathgap.description: Using a person's count from before earlier transfers or updates when evaluating a later relational statement.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model fails to track the temporal evolution of counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always use the most recent count for each person at the moment a relational statement is processed.
